# ACT_PHASE=C1-EVIDENCE
# EVIDENCE_KIND=semantic-authority-cset-classification
# THE DECISION: DOES aarch64EmitCSet OWN AN INDEPENDENT SEMANTIC
# DECISION, OR IS IT A C-OWNED MECHANICAL ADAPTER?
# THE ANSWER IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. The ACT explicitly forbids
# inferring a third authority from the fact that CSET produces
# observable assembly, and equally forbids predeclaring two
# authorities without checking all the original emission semantics.
# PART 1: THE SOURCE-LEVEL DECISION-CONTENT CENSUS
# The compiled PolyC detector counts, inside each function's whole
# definition, the occurrences of the constructs that could carry a
# CONDITION SELECTION.
site_id
SITE-A64-CC-FOR
column8: YES -- two switches (float and integer) selecting among the suffixes

column1: SITE-A64-CC-INV
column8: YES -- two switches (float and integer) selecting among the INVERSE suffixes

column1: SITE-A64-CSET
column8: NO -- no switch, no case, no IR_CMP reference; its entire semantic content is ONE call to aarch64CcFor

column1: # The CSET whole definition, byte for byte, is:
#   static void aarch64EmitCSet(IrCgCtx *ctx, IrCmpKind cmp, int is_float) {
#       aoStrCatFmt(ctx->buf, "cset    x0, %s\n\t", aarch64CcFor(cmp, is_float));
# The decision the site makes is: WHICH SUFFIX STRING is formatted
# into the host's assembly buffer. That decision is FULLY DETERMINED
# by aarch64CcFor's output. The remaining content -- the literal
# format string "cset    x0, %s\n\t", the register x0 and the
# separator -- is FIXED MECHANICAL FORMATTING with no condition in it.
# PART 2: THE EMPIRICAL CAUSAL EXPERIMENTS
# Three disposable detached worktrees, each with a full production
# compiler rebuild (the canonical `make all` bootstrap chain: stage0
# -> parser-padding subject -> production hcc). The witness is a real
# AArch64 emission: a comparison whose result has TWO uses, so the
# optimiser does NOT fuse it into IR_CMP_BR and the emitter takes the
# cset path. The pristine compiler emits exactly the assembly RECON03
# recorded ("cset x0, lt"), which reproduces the historical seam.
# THE ISOLATION MATRIX (each cell is the observed emitted suffix):
compiler
pristine
CSET-mutant (FOR table intact)
FOR-mutant (CSET site byte-identical)
INV-mutant
# WHAT THIS PROVES:
#   * A mutation confined ENTIRELY to the FOR table changes the CSET
#     emission (lt -> ge) while the CSET site itself is BYTE-IDENTICAL
#     (its 152-byte digest d915e499... / 8a1f2573... is unchanged).
#     Therefore the CSET output is FULLY DETERMINED by FOR's suffix:
#     the CSET site owns NO independent condition-code selection.
#   * A mutation confined ENTIRELY to the CSET site changes the CSET
#     emission (lt -> ne) while leaving the INV witness untouched.
#     This proves the CSET EMITTER PATH IS LIVE -- and nothing more.
#     It is exactly the "substituting a literal for the aarch64CcFor
#     call" case, which the ACT says proves emitter liveness and NOT
#     an independent condition-code selection.
#   * A mutation confined ENTIRELY to the INV table changes ONLY the
#     inverse branch (b.ge -> b.lt) and leaves the CSET emission
#     unchanged. FOR and INV are therefore SEPARATELY ATTRIBUTABLE.
# The assembly-file digests of the eight witness outputs corroborate
# the matrix independently of the text extraction:
#   m_pristine_cset.s    == m_mutant-inv_cset.s   (the INV mutation
#                                                    does not affect cset)
#   m_pristine_inv.s     == m_cset_inv.s == m_mutant-for_inv.s
#   m_cset_cset.s        != m_pristine_cset.s      (CSET is live)
#   m_mutant-for_cset.s  != m_pristine_cset.s      (FOR drives cset)
#   m_mutant-inv_inv.s   != m_pristine_inv.s       (INV is live)
# PART 3: THE PREDECESSOR'S OWN RECORDS AGREE
# RECON03's own evidence corroborates the classification, and this ACT
# quotes it rather than re-deriving it by assertion:
#   RECON03 c2/causal-experiments/SITE-A64-CC-CSET/site-isolation.tsv:
#     "ISOLATED (this site's mutation replaces the call to
#      aarch64CcFor with a constant, so the aarch64CcFor TABLE itself
#      is unchanged and the FOR site still emits cset x0, lt)"
#   RECON03 c2/causal-experiments/SITE-A64-CC-FOR/source-and-build.tsv:
#     "ADJACENT_SITE_CONTROL_OUTCOMES=... W-A64-CC-CSET CHANGED
#      (cset x0, ge, CMP_BAD) -- the CSET witness shares the
#      aarch64CcFor table and is therefore NOT an isolation control
#      for this site"
# The predecessor itself recorded that (a) the CSET mutation was a
# literal substitution for the FOR call, and (b) the CSET witness is
# COUPLED to the FOR table and is therefore not an isolation control.
# A witness that cannot isolate a site cannot establish that site as
# an independent authority.
# PART 4: THE SEMANTIC_DECISION_UNIQUE TEST
# The ACT requires a SEMANTIC_DECISION_UNIQUE=YES witness showing a
# source-backed choice distinguishable from FOR under FIXED FOR output.
site_id
SITE-A64-CC-FOR
column3: its own two switches select the suffix; a FOR mutation changes the cset emission

column1: SITE-A64-CC-INV
column3: its own two switches select the INVERSE suffix; an INV mutation changes only the inverse branch

column1: SITE-A64-CSET
column3: (1) zero switches, zero cases, zero IR_CMP references in its 152-byte definition; (2) its only decision input is aarch64CcFor's return value; (3) a FOR-only mutation changes its output with the CSET site byte-identical; (4) RECON03's own CSET mutation was a literal substitution for the FOR call; (5) RECON03's own FOR record says the CSET witness shares the FOR table and is not an isolation control
